terms.grammar: dīrēctum, neuter of dīrēctus, used as an adverb, with loquor
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections. Dīrēctus takes the long e of rēctus (Lachmann’s law).

sources: Lewis & Short: directus · Lewis & Short: loquor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).: p. 338.
